name: Halloumi Tabbouleh
steps: Rinse the bulgur wheat in running water until the water runs clear. Bring clean water to a boil in a saucepan and season with salt. Add the bulgur and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the water has absorbed. Cover and leave to steam for 2 minutes, then fluff the grains with a fork and allow to cool.

Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes in half, remove any stems and spoon out the seeds so you are left with just the flesh. Finely dice the flesh then scoop up the tomatoes and drain away any excess moisture. Place into a large mixing bowl.
Finely chop the spring onion and add into the bowl. Squeeze in the juice and zest of a lemon and season with salt and pepper. Mix everything together.
Time for the tahini dressing. In a cup mix together the tahini, grate in the garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Add water splash by splash until you have a nice creamy tahini dressing.

Slice the halloumi and add into a bowl. Season with olive oil, salt and pepper. Heat a non-stick frying pan on a medium-high heat and whack in the halloumi. Fry each piece of halloumi on both sides until golden brown and set aside.

While the halloumi is frying, finely chop your herbs. It is important not to bruise them so try to chop them as finely as possible on the first chop through so that you don’t have to go back and forth lots of times.
Add the herbs and the spices into the tomato bowl along with the cooled bulgur and pomegranate. Season with salt and pepper then drizzle with olive oil and toss together.
Immediately serve up the herby tabbouleh (you don't want to leave it sitting around for too long). Top with your golden halloumi, and drizzle over the tahini dressing.
